text:
Bitcoin slid into a sluggish $64,500–$65,000 consolidation range as markets digested Chair Kevin Warsh's inaugural Federal Reserve press conference. The Fed's widely anticipated decision to hold the federal funds rate at 3.50%–3.75%—driven by sticky 4.2% headline inflation and robust retail sales (+0.9%)—anchored the crypto Fear & Greed Index in "Extreme Fear" at 22.

Institutional capital flows revealed a stark intra-crypto rotation. Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of 1,543 BTC ($10 million), while Ethereum spot funds captured 9,361 ETH ($16.4 million) in net inflows as managers diversified away from pure-play Bitcoin exposure.

Wall Street's broader rotation mirrored this caution. As the Dow pushed record highs, technology and AI-linked equities faced selling pressure, highlighting a highly selective risk environment. Until the Fed signals a definitive pivot from its higher-for-longer regime, Bitcoin's correlation with the resilient U.S. dollar and elevated risk-free rates will remain the primary constraint on institutional digital asset allocation.
